name: Bias Blind Spot
description: People readily spot bias in other people while seeing their own judgments as comparatively objective. The mind gives itself a special exemption from the very distortions it recognizes elsewhere.
design_relevance_note: Directly relevant to research synthesis, prioritization debates, and design critique: teams can diagnose users, stakeholders, or other functions as biased while treating their own framing, sampling, and interpretation choices as neutral.
prevalence_note: Common in debiasing workshops, research-interpretation discussions, and cross-functional decision retrospectives, even if it is not one of the classic consumer-facing UX laws.

findings.description: Across three surveys and follow-up studies, people rated themselves as less susceptible to cognitive and motivational biases than others and treated their own self-assessments as objective, revealing a robust self-other asymmetry in perceived bias.
findings.source_title: The Bias Blind Spot: Perceptions of Bias in Self Versus Others

applications.title: Hansen et al.'s biased-strategy self-objectivity experiments
applications.description: Across 3 experiments, participants who were explicitly told to use a biased judgment strategy (e.g. focusing only on a test's weaknesses, or rating paintings using an admittedly one-sided method) went on to rate their own resulting judgments as relatively objective -- and in one experiment, participants' sense of their own objectivity actually grew stronger after using the biased strategy, not weaker. Knowingly using a biased method did not stop people from claiming, and apparently believing, that their conclusions were fair.
applications.industry_context: psychology research methodology (not a digital-product context)
applications.ethical_note: A research finding about self-perception with no persuasion or product-design dimension -- directly relevant to any design or research team's confidence that their own review/QA process is unbiased simply because they're aware bias is possible.
